base.description: Primary background color for the entire page, serving as the foundational layer that supports all other UI elements and creates a cohesive backdrop for the overall design.

progress-bar.description: To be used on progress-bar backgrounds.

primary.description: Base layer color applied to the majority of backgrounds, including containers, cards, and menus.

secondary.description: Secondary background color used for layered elements such as cards, containers, or overlays, providing depth and differentiation within the UI.

panel.description: Background color applied to panels, typically used for modular sections or sidebars, creating separation and structure within the interface.

action.description: Neutral color for interactive elements like buttons and icon links, designed to become more prominent upon interaction, indicating potential user actions without being overly emphasized in the default state.

gradient.description: This gradient transitions verticaly from the primary surface color token ($color.surface.primary) at the top (0%) to the secondary surface color token ($color.surface.secondary) at the bottom (100%).

input.description: Background color for input fields, checkboxes, radio buttons, and switches/toggles, designed to give the appearance of being cut out from the primary surface, creating a recessed effect.

input-error.description: Background color for the color.surface.input token that indicate an error state, providing a visually distinct and alerting appearance to highlight issues in user input.

primary.description: Foreground color for primary text and key content elements, optimized for readability and contrast against background surfaces, ensuring a clear visual hierarchy.

secondary.description: Foreground color for secondary text and supporting content elements, providing a subtle contrast against primary backgrounds to ensure legibility while maintaining a clear visual hierarchy.

tertiary.description: Foreground color for tertiary text and informational elements, offering low contrast against primary backgrounds to convey less critical information while preserving overall readability.

primary-inverted.description: Foreground color for primary text elements designed to provide an inverted appearance to the standard primary content color.

perma-black.description: A fixed black color used for text and essential content elements, ensuring maximum contrast and readability against light backgrounds.

perma-white.description: A fixed white color used for text and essential content elements, ensuring maximum contrast and readability against dark backgrounds

disabled.description: Color used for disabled text and non-interactive elements, indicating unavailability or inactive state, with reduced contrast to ensure clear differentiation from active content.

error.description: Color used to indicate error messages and alerts within the UI, providing high visibility and contrast to effectively communicate issues and capture user attention for corrective actions.

placeholder.description: Color used for placeholder text in input fields and text areas, offering a subtle contrast to indicate the absence of user input while maintaining legibility.

btn-disabled.description: Color for borders of disabled buttons, indicating an inactive state while ensuring clear differentiation from active buttons.

input.description: Color for borders of input fields, providing a clear outline to define interactive areas and enhance usability.

input-error.description: Color for borders of input fields in an error state, visually alerting users to issues with their input.

input-sucess.description: Color for borders of input fields indicating a successful state, providing positive feedback to users after correct input.

scrim.description: A semi-transparent color overlay used to dim background content, often applied when modals or dialogs are active, focusing user attention on foreground elements while still showing some background context.

navigation.description: Background overlay used for navigation panels, typically dimming surrounding content to prioritize navigation menus or drawers while retaining a cohesive interface.

tooltip-default.description: Background overlay applied to tooltips, providing a subtle backdrop that contrasts with the main UI to enhance tooltip visibility without overpowering surrounding elements.

gradient.description: A linear gradient overlay (0deg, from 40% black to transparent), often used to create depth or a fading effect on backgrounds, ensuring smooth transitions and clear visual separation between layered content.

gradient-primary-on-avatar-edit.description: A linear gradient overlay (0deg, from 70% to 100% of the primary surface color), used to subtly blend UI components or create a visual fade, ensuring consistent layering on primary surfaces.

default.description: Used as the background color for regular buttons in their default, non-interacted state with 11% opacity.

hover.description: Applied when regular buttons are hovered over, increasing opacity to 17% for interaction feedback.

disabled.description: Used for regular buttons in a disabled state with 5% opacity to indicate inactivity.
